author: TEDx Talks
description:
You wash your hands after using the bathroom, before eating and when caring for someone who is sick. But what about the object you touch thousands of times a day?

After witnessing healthcare workers use smartphones during the births of both his children, molecular biologist Dr Lotti Tajouri began investigating an overlooked hygiene risk hiding in plain sight. His research uncovered thousands of microorganisms living on mobile phones, including bacteria, viruses and drug-resistant pathogens capable of causing serious infections.

Drawing on research spanning hospitals, international travel and biosecurity, Lotti reveals why smartphones may be quietly undermining modern hygiene practices — and makes the case that if we treat our phones like a third hand, we should be cleaning them like one too. Dr Lotti Tajouri is a molecular biologist whose work focuses on infectious disease, biosecurity and the unseen microbial worlds humans interact with every day. His research spans public health,
title: Is your phone really dirtier than a toilet seat? | Lotti Tajouri | TEDxBrisbane

description: How do you find connection to the music of the past? Renaissance history comes alive in Monteverdi's L'Orfeo, one of history's first operas, in this heartfelt talk by high schooler Dylan Oh about the power of love.  Dylan Oh is a student at Riverdale Country School. During the 2025-2026 school year, he pursued an independent study on Monteverdi’s L’Orfeo and examined how one of the earliest operas uses music to express grief, longing, and the emotional complexity of human life. At Riverdale, he co-leads the Flume Ensemble, a student-led musical group that performs regularly at school and senior homes, and he is also a staff writer on the Riverdale Review. Outside of school, Dylan studies cello at Juilliard Pre-College and has a profound passion for exploring and sharing the historical and contemporary interpretations of classical music, particularly music from the Baroque Era. What happens when you go from front line amputee to Ironman finisher? You put your best foot forward! Eric McElvenny shares the four keys of resilience that allowed him to go from the frontlines serving in Afghanistan to finishing an Ironman under two years later. Description: We live under the dangerous delusion that we can isolate our health from the well-being of the planet and its animals. In this eye-opening talk, the speaker uncovers the hidden biological bridge connecting factory farms, street animals, and global health crises like pandemics and Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR).
Highlighting the flawed practice of mass culling and drawing inspiration from groundbreaking work like that of the late Dr. Naseem Salahuddin, the talk advocates for the One Health Approach—a framework proving that human health, animal welfare, and environmental stability are inseparable. By shifting our perspective from fear to empathy and scientific co-existence, protecting animal welfare becomes our ultimate shield against future public health disasters. Ahsan Iqbal is a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) student and the President of the One Health Society, a student-led initiative dedicated to advancing public health awareness. title: Why Beating Pandemics Starts with Protecting Animals | Ahsan Iqbal | TEDxTLHC

description:
In this TED talk, Archana Amlapure , CEO of Ojas Yoga and Wellness, Singapore , explores the hidden cost of modern work culture: Burnout , Depleted energy, Poor posture , and the growing “Stillness Gap.” Drawing from research and her own journey from corporate stress to yoga and wellness, she reveals why performance depends not only on time and effort, but on how well we protect our physical and mental energy. She introduces the simple MBR framework, Move, Breathe, Rest, three practical micro-resets that can be used anytime, even at a desk. Her message is clear: Healthier, Inspired, and Energised people create stronger organisations and more sustainable success for everyone.
